paragraphs.text: Stickler syndrome type VI is an autosomal recessive collagenopathy caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the COL9A3 gene, which encodes the alpha-3 chain of type IX collagen. Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) and Rad et al. (2022) found that the features seen in all reported patients were high myopia and moderate to severe or profound sensorineural hearing loss. Skeletal involvement, including epiphyseal or spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, varied more between patients, as did midface hypoplasia, vitreoretinal degeneration, retinal detachment, and cataract (Rad et al., 2022). Cleft palate had not been reported (Markova et al., 2021).

paragraphs.text: Faletra et al. (2014) described a family with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome. According to the summaries by Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) and Rad et al. (2022), the family was of Moroccan origin with first-cousin parents and had 3 affected sibs aged 4, 11, and 16 years. The sibs had moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss, moderate to high myopia, normal vitreous, midface hypoplasia, tibial rotation, mild irregularities of the capital femoral and metacarpal epiphyses, and pes planus. They also had moderate to severe intellectual disability, which Faletra et al. (2014) suggested was unrelated to the COL9A3 mutation (Hanson-Kahn et al., 2018).

paragraphs.text: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) reported a boy whose parents were third cousins from India. He failed his newborn hearing screen. At age 5 months, audiologic evaluation found moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss on the right and severe sensorineural hearing loss on the left, from 250 through 4,000 Hz. The hearing loss stayed stable. A CT scan of the temporal bones at 7 months showed only mild enlargement of the vestibular aqueducts. He had no myopia at 5 months. By 2 years he had myopia of -6.75 OD and -8 OS, and by 12 years this had progressed to -10.75 OD and -11.25 OS. No vitreous abnormalities were noted. Femoral and tibial bowing were present at birth. Radiographs at 6 years showed flattening of the acetabula, slightly flattened proximal femoral epiphyses, irregularity of the medial distal femoral epiphyses, and mild platyspondyly. Growth parameters were normal. Speech was initially delayed, which was attributed to the hearing loss, and intelligence was normal. Autoimmune hypothyroidism was diagnosed at age 10 years. No hearing loss, myopia, or skeletal anomalies were reported in the parents or in his older sister.

paragraphs.text: Nixon et al. (2019) studied 4 families with recessive Stickler syndrome caused by type IX collagen gene variants. One family had 2 patients with a COL9A3 variant. All 6 patients in the study were highly myopic, with congenital megalophthalmos and abnormal, hypoplastic vitreous gel, and all had sensorineural hearing loss. One patient had severe arthropathy. Rad et al. (2022) and Markova et al. (2021) reported further details of the COL9A3 sibs. They were aged 18 and 20 years and had severe sensorineural hearing loss. The older sib had refraction of -23 D in each eye at age 20 years and severe arthropathy of the shoulders and hip. This sib required a wheelchair, had undergone surgery for scoliosis, and had narrowing of the articular space in both knees on radiographs; the younger sib had none of these signs. Rad et al. (2022) also stated that Nixon et al. (2019) observed mild Stickler phenotypes in carrier parents.

paragraphs.text: Markova et al. (2021) reported a boy born of healthy nonconsanguineous parents; the pregnancy was complicated by oligohydramnios and fetal growth retardation. At age 1 month he had adductor spasm, hip dysplasia confirmed by ultrasound, and bilateral absence of ossification centers. Congenital high bilateral myopia was found at 3 months, and bilateral sensorineural hearing loss of grade 3 to 4 was diagnosed at 11 months. He had delayed speech development. Spine radiographs at 1 and 3 years showed spina bifida occulta of the sacral vertebrae, mild platyspondyly, and kyphosis with the apex at T11. Radiographs of the lower limbs at 3 years showed enlarged joint spaces, flattened and irregular femoral heads, broadened and shortened femoral necks, coxa valga, and flattened distal femoral epiphyses. Ophthalmic assessment found peripheral pigment rearrangement, small whitish dystrophic foci, multiple vitreous floaters, and a preretinal membrane in the right eye; the electroretinogram was normal. When examined at 2 years 5 months, he had a valgus knee deformity, waddling gait, rapid fatigability, and pain in the lower limb joints. His height was 88 cm (25th-50th percentile). He had a slightly flattened nasal bridge, small nose, mild midface hypoplasia, high palate, lumbar lordosis, limited hip abduction, long fingers, prominent knee joints, genu valgum, and planovalgus foot deformity. Markova et al. (2021) considered this a more severe presentation than previously reported, with early-onset arthropathy and vitreoretinal degeneration.

paragraphs.text: Rad et al. (2022) reported 5 affected individuals from 3 unrelated consanguineous Iranian families, all with first-cousin parents. The proband in family 1 was a 28-year-old woman. She had high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with empty vitreous, multiple lattice degenerations, and retinal pigmentary changes, together with severe progressive sensorineural hearing loss. She had knee pain, but joint examination and radiographs were normal, and she lacked typical Stickler craniofacial features. The 2 affected sibs in family 2 were aged 65 and 57 years. Both had high myopia and had undergone multiple vitreoretinal surgeries for recurrent rhegmatogenous retinal detachment due to advanced vitreoretinal degeneration. Both also had cataract, profound progressive sensorineural hearing loss, and a herniated cervical disc. The older sib was blind without light perception. The 2 affected sibs in family 3, a boy aged 11.8 years and his sister aged 3.1 years, had myopia, congenital moderate to severe progressive sensorineural hearing loss, and spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia. They also had pes planus, a depressed nasal bridge, and anteverted nares; midface hypoplasia and downslanting palpebral fissures were more pronounced in the sister. The boy had knee pain, genu valgum, irregular femoral epiphyses, flattened femoral heads, short metacarpals, and a broad big toe. None of the 5 patients had intellectual disability or short stature. Rad et al. (2022) noted that the older patients in family 2 had milder skeletal findings than the younger patients in family 3.
